Object Replication Example

gxObjRepl replicates objects from a primary to a copy; a planned switch makes the copy the primary, and the old primary its copy. Windows and Linux.

What It Shows

Object replication with gxObjRepl (DataReel 7.4), between Windows and Linux nodes in both directions. Two nodes, the folders WORK/a and WORK/b, run in this one program; the copy serves in a thread, so the same program runs on both platforms:

  1. a is the primary and b the copy. a commits three transactions of notes (Begin(), NewId(), Put(), Commit()) and Drain()s them to b, which reads the newest one back with Get().
  2. Both stop. gxObjRepl::Digest() of each folder: the same objects.
  3. A planned switch: Takeover() makes b the primary at epoch 2, and Rejoin() makes a its copy. a's copy had every commit, so no full send is needed.
  4. b commits two more transactions and drains them to a; the digests agree again.

The nodes use mutual TLS: the copy listens with the server certificate and allows the primary's client certificate by its CN. Each node keeps its own file addresses and indexes; only objects travel. The administrator's view of the same steps, with the objrepl tool, is in the replication administrator's guide.

Running It

Make the certificates once, then run it on an empty folder (Linux shown; on Windows the same with the Release folder):

utils/objrepl/objrepl_certs.sh pki --copy-host 127.0.0.1 --apply
mkdir work
BUILD/examples/object_replication pki work        # PORT 24750 and 24751 by default

Sample Output

1. a is the primary, b the copy: three commits
  primary: last commit 3, the copy has 3
  the copy reads its newest note: "note 3.1"
2. both stopped: the same objects?
  a: objects 6 digest 583f8ee882c4cbce
  b: objects 6 digest 583f8ee882c4cbce
3. a planned switch: b takes over, a rejoins as its copy
  work/b is primary at epoch 2 (applied 3)
  work/a is a copy at epoch 1, following on from seq 3 (its copy had every commit: no full send)
4. b is the primary, a the copy: two more commits
  b is the primary at epoch 2
  primary: last commit 5, the copy has 5
  the copy reads its newest note: "note 5.1"
  a: objects 10 digest ebdadaf76f634365
  b: objects 10 digest ebdadaf76f634365
OK: 10 notes replicated, then a switch, the same objects on both nodes

The digests change with the ids, which carry the epoch and a counter; they are always equal between a and b. The exit code is 0 when every step worked. tests/run_tests.sh runs it (object_replication). Back to the example programs.

Source

examples/oodb/object_replication.cpp, one source file built by examples/CMakeLists.txt as object_replication and run by tests/run_tests.sh. The comment at the top of the file describes each step. Back to the example programs.
